nodes.title: Rejected: emitting JavaScript u-flag regex patterns (\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}) in tool JSON schemas.
nodes.tried: shared/validate.ts str({pattern}) copied pattern.source into the schema; five intake tools used a Unicode-class key pattern.
nodes.broke: Azure OpenAI rejected the whole request ("is not a 'regex'") whenever an offered tool carried it: 21 of 48 Operator bench tasks never reached the model on either gpt-4.1 or gpt-4.1-mini (research/2026-10-23/benches/README.md, bug 1).

nodes.title: Tool schemas carry only portable regex patterns: no flags, no \p{…}, lookbehind, named groups or \u{…}. A non-portable pattern stays a server-side check and the schema describes it in words. tests/tool-schemas-portable.test.ts walks every registered tool.
nodes.reverse_if: Every provider the product supports accepts Unicode property classes in function schemas, verified by a request to each.

nodes.title: Every tool and plan result reaches the Operator's model with an outcome first (DONE / NOT DONE / WAITING FOR APPROVAL / UNKNOWN; plans say n of m steps ran plus a notDone list), the compactor always keeps it, and the conduct rules say NOT DONE means nothing changed.
nodes.rationale: On the 2026-10-23 bench a reply claimed an edit that had been refused; plan results began with status 'planned' even when every step was refused.
nodes.reverse_if: A real-model re-run shows false success claims persist at the same rate; then the cause is elsewhere (e.g. the model ignores tool results) and needs a code-level check on the reply.

nodes.title: agent.create from a description: the drafting prompt states field types (mirrorCaller true or false), and a draft that fails validation gets exactly one repair turn carrying the validator's message; a second failure is refused naming the field and the accepted form. Code never guesses a value.
nodes.rationale: Both gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini returned mirrorCaller as a language code; strict validation refused every draft (bench bug 2).
nodes.reverse_if: Repair turns rarely succeed in bench re-runs (cost without benefit), or a structured-output mode makes invalid drafts impossible.

nodes.title: The Operator bench counts a turn that ended in a model error as a fail and reports 'reached the model' separately (count and pass rate with CI); a clarifying request counts as asking with or without a question mark.
nodes.rationale: On 2026-10-23, 5 refusal and injection tasks per model scored PASS only because the provider refused the request and nothing changed; imperative clarifications were scored as no question.
nodes.reverse_if: Never for the model-error rule; widen the clarification detector if real replies show other phrasings.

events.details: Six fixes from the first real-model Operator bench: portable schema patterns, plan tool-name mapping, typed drafting prompt with one repair turn, JSON Pointer brief.edit paths, outcome-first tool results, and bench grading (model error = fail, reached-model reported, clarifications counted). Ready for the re-run.
